name: Skip link
description: A link at the very start of the page that jumps past the Header and Navigation to the Main content. It usually stays hidden until it receives keyboard focus.
summary: Lets keyboard users jump past navigation

elements.name: Link text
elements.description: Names the destination, e.g. "Skip to main content"

elements.name: Target
elements.description: The element with the matching id, usually <main>

elements.name: Extra links
elements.description: A second skip link, e.g. to Search; keep the set short

usageNotes: Make it the first focusable element in <body>, so the first Tab press reaches it. It is the usual way to meet WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.
Hide it in a way that keeps it focusable, such as the Visually hidden pattern, and reveal it on :focus. display: none and the hidden attribute remove it for keyboard users too.
When focused it must be visible with a clear focus indicator (WCAG 2.4.7) and not covered by a sticky Header (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured).
Point it at an element with a matching id, usually Main. Adding tabindex="-1" to the target makes focus move there reliably, so the next Tab continues from the content.
Use text that names the destination. One link is usually enough; a long list of skip links brings back the problem it was meant to solve.
